lots.what_it_is: Box of mixed ornamental china and bric-a-brac: Japanese export cups and saucers (geisha and lithophane-style), a Nippon-style hand-painted rose and gilt dish, Capodimonte-style horse and carriage and crinoline lady figurines, floral teacups, a red plate, a set of carved wooden salad servers and a few small vases. The only local-interest piece is a white scalloped crested souvenir dish with the Tasmanian arms (two thylacine supporters) and a small caption that appears to read LAUNCESTON TASMANIA, probably early 20th century German or Japanese crested ware. No maker's marks visible.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: no sold, unsold or asking entries. Gowans API rechecked today for launceston dish, tasmania crest, souvenir china and crested china: no matching past lots. WebSearch is capped for this turn, so no Armitage past results could be searched.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Generic mixed china of this type typically makes very little at Tasmanian rooms; the Tasmanian crest souvenir dish is the only piece with any collector pull and on its own is a small-money item.
lots.confidence_reason: No price evidence at all; no maker's marks visible; crested dish caption only partly legible.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 3: scalloped gilt-rimmed white dish with the Tasmanian coat of arms, two thylacines rampant either side of a shield, caption under the arms reads roughly LAUNCESTON TASMANIA (small and blurred). Photo 4: Nippon-style hand-painted rose dish with heavy gilt and handle, Japanese geisha plates and cups. Photo 2: Capodimonte-style figural carriage group, crinoline figures with lace skirts. No backstamps visible in any photo.
lots.condition: Unknown; no obvious breaks seen but most pieces are stacked and partly hidden, so chips and crazing cannot be ruled out.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a backstamp on the Launceston Tasmania crested dish (e.g. Germany, Foley, Arcadian) and is it free of chips? Any marks on the rose-painted gilt dish (Nippon)?
